problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Which of the following pairs could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y)?$

- ${f}_{x}(x,y)=4x+{y}^{2}$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=4xy-y$
- ${f}_{x}(x,y)=2x+y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=x+\sqrt{y}$
- ${f}_{x}(x,y)=2xy+{y}^{2}$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)={x}^{2}y+2x$

feedback.problem:
Suppose that a function $f(x,y,z)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ and that

$$
\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂z}=3{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)+3x{y}^{2}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)+3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)
$$

Evaluate the following expression at the point $(\pi ,-1,1):$

$$
\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂z∂y∂y}+\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂y∂z∂z}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
As the higher order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂z∂y∂y} & =\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂y∂y∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂z}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)+3x{y}^{2}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)+3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =6y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)+6xyz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)-3{x}^{3}{z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy).\end{aligned}
$$

In addition, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂y∂z∂z} & =\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂z∂y∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂z}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(3{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)+3x{y}^{2}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)+3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =3x{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)+3x{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}z\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)+6{x}^{2}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate both partial derivatives at the point $(\pi ,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂z∂y∂y}{|}_{(\pi ,-1,1)} & =6(-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+6(\pi )(-1)(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-3(\pi )^{3}(1)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )=6\pi  \\ \frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂y∂z∂z}{|}_{(\pi ,-1,1)} & =3(\pi )(-1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+3(\pi )(-1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-3(\pi )^{2}(-1)^{2}(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+6(\pi )^{2}(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )=-6\pi -6{\pi }^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂z∂y∂y}{|}_{(\pi ,-1,1)}+\frac{{∂}^{3}f}{∂y∂z∂z}{|}_{(\pi ,-1,1)} & =6\pi +(-6\pi -6{\pi }^{2})=-6{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
